item.title: Spring Boot OAuth2 + JWT: End-to-End Zero-Trust API Security
item.description: Zero-trust API security means every request is validated independently — no session state, no “trusted network” assumptions. A JWT bearer token is issued by an authorisation server, signed cryptographically, and validated on every API call. The API never calls back to the authorisation server during validation; it verifies the token’s signature locally. This guide covers the complete setup: dependencies, resource server configuration, token validation (both symmetric and asymmetric), extracting claims, role-based access control, method-level security, and the Spring Security 7 changes that break existing setups.
